text: Refactoring is the process of improving the structure of your code without changing what it does. Instead of adding new features, you focus on making the existing code cleaner and easier to understand. For example, you might break a long function into smaller parts or rename unclear variables. The main goal is to improve readability for future developers, including yourself. Over time, messy code creates what programmers call "technical debt." This means the code works now, but it is slow and risky to change later. By refactoring regularly, you pay off that debt and keep your project healthy. Remember, the behavior stays exactly the same—only the inside becomes better.
